traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Trillium ovatum: stems 30 cm to 50 cm tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Trillium ovatum: leaves 5 cm to 15 cm long.

traits.shoot_leaves.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), genus Trillium: 3 leaves in a whorl at the top of the stem, which grows in one season.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Abrams, Illustrated Flora of the Pacific States vol. 1 (1923), genus Trillium: unbranched herbs with three leaves whorled at the top of the stem, below the single flower (single long-stalked leaves sometimes rise from the rootstock).

traits.leaves_per_whorl.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), genus Trillium: three leaves in the whorl.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a woodland lily: a single stem with a whorl of three broad leaves and one white, three-petalled flower above them. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.33 m tall at 8 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark green leaves; white flowers that age to pink.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: FloraPNW's treatment of Trillium, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): three green, persistent sepals and three petals; 6 stamens; ovary superior; an iNaturalist guide in the Flora of North America's style adds petals 1.5 to 7 cm, sepals 15 to 50 mm, and three stigmas, so three carpels.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.note: Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5): three white petals between three green sepals, six stamens and a pistil of three carpels, from the characters by the rules at the flowering plants; the sepals three quarters of a petal's length by hand (as search results quote them; the pages themselves were not read).

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
